title: current_plans.sql

spec.text: One row per active customer: their current plan (from their most recent plan_changes row) and lifetime paid amount (sum of their succeeded payments, 0 if none). Customers whose most recent change is a cancellation are excluded. If two changes share the same changed_at, the higher id is the most recent.

context: PostgreSQL 16. plan_changes(id, customer_id, plan, action in ('start','upgrade','downgrade','cancel'), changed_at timestamptz). payments(id, customer_id, amount_cents, status in ('succeeded','failed','refunded'), paid_at). Customers have many plan changes and many payments; trial customers have no payments. Batch imports often write several plan_changes rows with the same changed_at.

files.content:
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT
        pc.customer_id,
        pc.plan,
        pc.action,
        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY pc.customer_id
            ORDER BY pc.changed_at DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM plan_changes pc
    WHERE pc.action <> 'cancel'
),
paid AS (
    SELECT
        p.customer_id,
        SUM(p.amount_cents) OVER (PARTITION BY p.customer_id) AS lifetime_cents
    FROM payments p
    WHERE p.status = 'succeeded'
)
SELECT
    l.customer_id,
    l.plan,
    COALESCE(pd.lifetime_cents, 0) AS lifetime_cents
FROM latest l
LEFT JOIN paid pd ON pd.customer_id = l.customer_id
WHERE l.rn = 1
ORDER BY l.customer_id;
